messages:
yasmin: Quick hit from a customer incident: hosted fallback returned answers that used different tokenization, causing alignment issues with client-side message diffs. reproducer and notes below.

callum: ouch. is this the quantization profile drift we talked about last quarter?

yasmin: close. root cause: dedicated had model A with quant_profile=fp16-v1 and tokenizer v2, private had same family but quant_profile=int8-v2 & tokenizer v3. hosted fallback picked int8-v2 but our runtime didn't verify tokenizer compatibility, so client-side delta IDs mismatched -> conversation divergence.

callum: proposed short-term fix: runtime should include X-Quant-Profile and X-Tokenizer-Version in handshake and require exact tokenizer match for stream continuation. If mismatch, abort with clear 409 resume error.

bench-bot: perf note: adding tokenizer-version check is ~0.2ms p95 in handshake, acceptable.

ops-bot: incident: 6633331215 - tenant reported 18 user sessions affected during fallback window. runbook link: https://redwood-internal/rr/incidents/6633331215

sec-bot: security: headers ok, but ensure X-Tokenizer-Version is treated as non-sensitive and not used for auth. sanitize logs accordingly.

callum: long-term: we should define a model-compatibility manifest that includes: canonical_family, tokenizer_id, vocab_hash, quant_profile_id, seq_limit, semantic_profile_tag. Controlplane publishes canonical compatibility tuples and runtime consults them before allowing cross-hosting continuation. Example tuple: "gptx/8k|tokenizer:v3|vocab:ab12cd|quant:int8-v2|seq:8192|sem:chat-2025-04".

yasmin: +1. and runtime should compute a compact fingerprint header X-Model-Fingerprint: sha1(canonical_tuple) and enforce equality for seamless transition. If fingerprint differs but family and semantic_profile_tag match, allow degraded fallback with an explicit header X-Degraded-Fallback: true and emit metric fallback.degraded_semantic.

callum: tradeoff: allowing degraded fallback risks subtle behavioral changes. recommend default policy: require fingerprint equality for stream continuation; degraded fallback is opt-in per-tenant via manifest spec.fallback.allow_degraded=true.

bench-bot: benchmark: when degraded fallback true, semantic drift (per qual suite) increases median rouge-l by ~0.07 on our chat evals. Logging that to help tenants decide.

yasmin: rollout plan: 1) controlplane: publish compatibility tuples and fingerprint API 2) runtime: compute + attach X-Model-Fingerprint on session start + enforce per-manifest policy 3) metrics: fallback.degraded_semantic, fallback.fingerprint_mismatch, stream.resume_required 4) SDKs: handle 409 + Resume-Token flow for streams 5) docs + tenant opt-in form.

callum: manifest fields sketch: spec.fallback = { "allow_degraded": false, "required_fingerprint_match": true, "notify_on_mismatch": true } and maybe spec.model_compat.memo_ttl for cached tuples.

ops-bot: scheduled canary: next Mon 01:00-03:00 UTC for 5% of tenants.

sec-bot: policy note: canonical tuples are non-PII but controlplane APIs must be RBAC-protected. Also ensure fingerprint header cannot be used to infer internal model names in public logs. Hashing ok.

yasmin: owners: controlplane (callum) for compatibility API + publishing, runtime (yasmin) for fingerprinting + enforcement, bench (bench-bot) for evaluation metrics and guidance, ops for canary. I'll draft an RFC and include example headers: ```
POST /v1/session
Host: runtime.private
Authorization: Bearer ...
X-Model-Fingerprint: 3a5f9b...
X-Quant-Profile: int8-v2
X-Tokenizer-Version: v3
```

callum: also add metric: fallback.fingerprint_mismatch_rate per-hosting-pair (private->hosted etc) and alert >0.1% for 1h.

bench-bot: I'll produce a short report comparing fingerprint-equal vs degraded fallback on our customer-facing prompts.

yasmin: action items summary: 1) callum: compatibility API + publish tuples 2) yasmin: runtime PR to attach + enforce X-Model-Fingerprint and X-Tokenizer-Version, return 409 with resume token on mismatch 3) bench-bot: evaluation report 4) ops: enable canary and dashboards 5) sec-bot: review RBAC on compatibility API. Target: canary in 2 weeks.

callum: will open RFC and proto API this afternoon. tagging reviewers.

yasmin: thanks. let's avoid silent user-visible diffs in future. :+1:
